lesson.subtitle: Lesson 16 -- Timelines and Deadlines
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 16 -- Timelines and Deadlines
lesson.grammar_point: present continuous for future arrangements and by for deadlines

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: To start a project or a meeting
The latest time or date to finish something
The moment when the finished work is given to the client
To move an event to a later date
An important point or stage in a project
Happening as planned, with no delay

vocab.text: A deadline and a milestone are not the same thing. A milestone is a point you celebrate on the way, like the end of the foundations; the deadline is the date you cannot pass. A project can miss a milestone and still meet the deadline, if the next phase is on track.

reading.rtitle: Schedule Update: East Side Pumping Stations, Phase Two
paras: Here is where we are. Phase one, the design, is finished, and the client approved it last Friday, so the project is on track. We are kicking off phase two on Monday, March 3. The contractor's crew is arriving on site at seven, and the excavation for Station 1 is starting the same week. The first milestone is the foundations: they must be finished by April 11.

Station 2 is a different story. The supplier is two weeks behind schedule with the pumps, so we are pushing back the installation to May 19. The deadline for the client does not change: the electrical work must be complete by June 30, and the handover is happening on August 29. Thiago is visiting the site on March 12, and he is sending the updated schedule to the utility by the end of that week.

reading.prompt: What is the main purpose of this update?
choices: To complain about the supplier and ask for a new one
To tell the team the dates of phase two and what changed for Station 2
To explain how a pumping station works

items: The design of the project is still not approved.
The text says the client approved the design last Friday.
The foundations of Station 1 must be finished by April 11.
The text says the first milestone is the foundations, and they must be finished by April 11.
Because of the pumps, the handover is moving to a later date.
The installation is pushed back to May 19, but the handover is still happening on August 29.
A new engineer asks what is happening on site next week. Explain the plans with the present continuous.
The supplier calls: the pumps are late again. Tell Rachel what you are pushing back, and what does not change.
Rachel asks for the new schedule. Tell her when you are sending it, with by.

practice.title: Turn each calendar note into a sentence. Use am, is or are plus -ing, or by for a deadline.
items: Monday 7 a.m. -- crew arrives on site
Safety reports -- not later than Wednesday

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: The crew is arriving on site at seven on Monday.
The inspector is visiting the site on Thursday.
The safety reports must be ready by Wednesday.
We are pushing back the pump installation to May 19.
answerkey.note: These are models, not the only correct answers. Any natural sentence with am, is or are plus -ing for the plan, and by for the deadline, works.

items.situation: Rachel asks when phase two starts. It is booked for Monday.
tips: It is in the calendar: use are plus -ing.
Use the phrasal verb for start: kick off.

items.situation: Your manager asks when the safety reports must be ready. The answer is not later than Wednesday.
The pumps are late, so the installation moves to a later date.
tips: Use the phrasal verb that means move to a later date.
We are ... the installation to May 19.

items.situation: The client wants to know if Station 1 has any delay. It does not.
tips: Use the expression for happening as planned.
Station 1 is ... for the first milestone.

items.situation: Ask Rachel about her plans for next week: is she visiting the site?
tips: Question with a plan: Are you plus -ing?
Finish with the time: next week.

listenings.text: Hi Thiago, it's Rachel. A quick update before the weekend. The client called this morning, and they are moving the progress meeting from Tuesday to Thursday, so we are presenting the schedule on Thursday at ten. I need your slides by Wednesday at noon, please. Also, the crew is not working on Friday, because of the holiday, so the excavation is starting a day later. That is fine, we are still on track for the first milestone. I am flying to Brazil on the twentieth, and I am visiting the site with you on the twenty-second. Talk soon.

Good morning, everyone, this is Dave, the site manager. Here is the plan for next week. On Monday we are closing the north road, so please use the east gate. The concrete trucks are arriving on Tuesday and Wednesday, early in the morning. On Thursday the inspector from the utility is visiting, and all the safety reports must be ready by Wednesday night. If you need a day off next month, tell me by Friday. That is all. Have a safe week.

extra_audio.text: First, the client approves the design, and phase one is finished. Then, the team kicks off phase two, and the crew arrives on site. After that, the foundations of Station 1 are finished by April 11. Next, the pumps for Station 2 are installed on May 19, two weeks later than planned. Finally, the handover happens on August 29.
